atlases.prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Create one production-ready raster texture atlas for the Working Stockyard screen of a historical strategy game. EXACT layout: 2 columns and 3 rows, six equally-sized cells in a 1536 by1024 landscape image. Uniform warm pale ivory/parchment background across the whole atlas (#f1e8d6 feel), no lines or frames. Match refined painterly realistic material specimen illustrations: rich tactile detail, restrained natural vivid color, three-quarter slightly elevated view, soft daylight from upper left, delicate contact shadows. Each isolated specimen/pile centered within its own cell, fills about75% of cell width and70% of cell height, ample clean margin so nothing crosses a cell boundary. Every object entirely visible. No text, names, numbers, letters, icons, labels, UI, watermark or decorative elements. These are actual raw resources, not finished tools, ingots or machinery. All six cells must be present in precisely this reading order: TOP LEFT: knapped and unknapped dark smoky grey flint nodules with sharp waxy chipped faces. TOP RIGHT: a small mound of naturally crystalline off-white rock salt with a few clear cubic crystals. MIDDLE LEFT: a gathered bunch of green medicinal leaves, small flowers and tangled roots tied simply with fiber. MIDDLE RIGHT: cut blocks and crumbled pieces of dark brown fibrous peat, visible plant fibers. BOTTOM LEFT: a small pile of creamy beige rough limestone chunks with chalky porous fracture surfaces. BOTTOM RIGHT: a low mound of fine pale golden quartz sand with fine individual grains and no vessel.
